label: I-3 CONFIRMED and widened: a whole-.skilled/ grep for CODE_QUALITY_RESULT, checklists_loaded and checker_outputs returns exactly three matches, all in the producer file at sk-code-quality/SKILL.md lines 210, 215 and 216, and zero in sk-code-review, .skilled/agents, .skilled/commands or the hub router files, so no framework file names a reader for the quality gate's advisory envelope; a reader added only inside the review packet would leave @review and @deep-review with the same hole.

U-9 CONFIRMED as written and REFINED in consequence: check-review-findings.js parses only number and hasCase (line 52) with CASE_LINE as its only content regex (line 23), and none of the 21 packet-wide matches for riskScore, Scope proof, Finding class or scopeProof land under scripts/, but the manual playbook does consume the fields as pass/fail criteria (class-of-bug-vs-instance-only.md:33 'FAIL if no scopeProof is provided'; p0-blocker-with-file-line.md:49 'Add findingClass and scopeProof') and the fix-completeness asset requires a finding class table, so the fields are un-automated rather than un-consumed and U-9's implied remedy of demoting them would delete a contract the playbook depends on.

E-3 PARTIALLY CONFIRMED and partly NOT TESTED: hub-router.json:11 defines the surface relationship as one-directional read-only evidence ordered after the workflow mode, which is the structural basis for a surface needing nothing back, but the same line is the only statement of the relationship and names no fields, so no surface-to-review payload schema exists and E-3's bounded-checks-and-scope-hints handoff remains a proposal; the review-side requirements resting on I-7 and I-8, and the mode-registry.json:18 citation, were not re-opened this iteration.

DERIVED: I-3, U-9 and E-3 share one shape, a documented producer with no declared consumer side, which suggests a single consumer-side contract file naming what each receiver must read rather than three separate fixes; a live quality-then-review run with a real user surface would confirm whether the runtime bridges any of the three informally.
